A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same aL-SAR research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, algorithms, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and several internally inconsistent descriptions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and multimodal continual-learning experiments, computational measurements, component ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical experiments and reports additional concept-answering and forgetting results, including Table 9 and Appendix A.25.

M1.justification: The main equations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, v1 A.17 updates an EMA of pairwise gradient cosine similarities, whereas v2 A.18 describes maintaining EMA class-wise gradients before forming similarities. This conflicts with the retained pseudocode, leaving unclear whether the procedure changed or the expanded explanation is inconsistent.

E1.justification: v2 Table 9 adds evaluated Bongard-HOI concept answering alongside the existing Bongard-OpenWorld concept-answering task. Multimodal learning itself was already evaluated in v1. The other dataset coverage remains, including ImageNet disjoint evaluation in the unlimited-memory appendix.

E2.justification: Matched retained comparisons preserve their comparator sets, including REMIND/PTLF/EGERIA for freezing, MIR/ASER for retrieval, and TriRE/SparCL for efficient CL. The latter comparison is relocated. The additional evaluations reuse existing comparators, including no freezing for concept answering.

E3.justification: The reported multimodal protocol changes from 500 memory samples to unlimited memory and from three to two support images per positive/negative set for Bongard-OpenWorld. Its concept-answering evaluation changes from CIDEr to GPT-based scoring; Bongard-HOI concept answering uses accuracy. New forgetting evaluations introduce Flast and KLR. These materially alter experimental conditions and outcome measurement.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.25 systematically compares forgetting across computational budgets on CIFAR-10/100 Gaussian and disjoint streams, with an additional ImageNet Gaussian comparison in Table 22. This adds direct retention analysis beyond the accuracy measurements, component ablations, architectural tests and toy analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds except for ImageNet, Welch's t-test at significance level 0.05, and the same uncertainty and significance-display conventions. No changed run count or new statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises aL-SAR's ImageNet Gaussian AAUC/Alast from 33.94/38.02 to 33.24/35.02 and removes the finite-memory disjoint results. Tables 3 and 9 replace multimodal scores and computational measurements under revised conditions, so these are not same-setting gains. v2 also adds Bongard-HOI concept-answering results and extensive forgetting results in Figure 18/Table 22.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the Fisher-information derivation, freezing criterion and retrieval definitions. No theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation is added or removed. The newly adopted forgetting metrics are empirical evaluation additions without new mathematical development.

C1.justification: The total-resource-budget argument, two-component contribution and principal efficiency/performance claims remain. v2 foregrounds multimodal validation in the abstract, but v1 already claims and demonstrates this application in Section 4.2; it does not introduce a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains smaller freezing savings on concept-answering tasks through their greater complexity and attributes reduced forgetting at larger budgets to more thorough learning of previous data. The ImageNet disjoint-specific interpretation is removed. Existing limitations concerning recurrent networks and memory efficiency remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository link stating that implementations, data splits and baselines are available. It adds the GPT evaluation prompt and expands gradient-selection/update documentation. The latter expansion has the unresolved inconsistency noted under M1; most existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds introductory references such as McCloskey and Cohen, Seo et al., and Wu et al., plus Chaudhry et al. for forgetting and Yu et al. for multimodal evaluation. The CIDEr and Verwimp references disappear. The substantive replay-learning and layer-freezing positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally rewritten and expanded, existing multimodal validation is highlighted in the abstract, and several appendix subsections are reordered. Affiliations, publication headers, reproducibility wording and acknowledgments change. Most methodological prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper-wide switch to ICLR formatting changes typography, text width, figure/table sizing and float placement. Table 1 loses its ImageNet disjoint columns, Table 9 expands to two concept-answering tasks, and a boxed evaluation prompt plus Figure 18/Table 22 are added. Existing plots otherwise retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful forgetting evidence, another concept-answering evaluation and stated code access. However, its expanded similarity-update account conflicts with Algorithm 1, and new evaluation reporting is inconsistent: A.13 names both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, while Table 22 prints 947,128 TFLOPs for aL-SAR versus 114,014 for baselines. These unresolved issues limit reproducibility and interpretation of the added evidence, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
